subject: Deployment mode decision: hosted vs dedicated vs private — next steps
messages:

Subject: Deployment mode decision: hosted vs dedicated vs private — next steps

Hi Oliver / Nina,

Thanks again for the call today — good discussion. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can get you a concrete Dedicated sizing recommendation and a Hosted vs Dedicated decision tradeoff: 

Summary of ParcelAI profile (as we understood it):
- Use case: document ingestion + LLM routing/classification for last-mile routing and returns automation
- Latency target: <= 120ms p95 for interactive routes; batch processing acceptable overnight
- Traffic: short bursts during peak hours, larger nightly batch jobs
- Security: VPC + SOC2 / PHI considerations requested

Deployment options and quick guidance:
1) Hosted API: fastest to launch; recommended if you need rapid testing and no strict VPC/SOC2 requirement. Cost higher per token at scale but minimal ops overhead.
2) Dedicated capacity (recommended baseline): reserved GPU pool with predictable throughput and data isolation. Best fit if you need consistent latency during peak bursts and want unit cost control.
3) Private (VPC or on-prem): for full control and compliance. Longer lead time and procurement overhead.

Dedicated sizing notes we want to confirm with you (we'll size more precisely in the workshop):
- Candidate GPU types: H100 80GB (best latency + throughput for long contexts), A100 80GB (balanced price/perf), L40S or L4 for lower-cost inference on short contexts (quantized models).
- TPS targets: you mentioned bursts — we need explicit numbers. For example: 250 TPS peak / 60 TPS sustained maps to X GPUs in our initial model (see below).
- Concurrency: estimate 6-12 concurrent streams per A100 for 512-token workloads; H100 can support higher concurrency for longer sequences.
- Token mix: please confirm percent short (<256), medium (256-1024), long (>1024). This materially changes memory/KV cache and batching plans.
- Optimization levers: dynamic batching, KV caching, quantization (4-bit) — we can show cost/latency tradeoffs in the workshop.

Preliminary scenarios (ballpark, subject to confirmation):
- Conservative (low cost): 3x A100 80GB + autoscaling burst allowance -> expected steady 50-70 TPS, handle 200 TPS short bursts with queueing and fallbacks.
- Performance (low-latency peak): 4x H100 80GB -> target ~220-260 TPS with p95 in target range for 512-token median.
- Hybrid: 2x H100 for latency-critical endpoints + 4x L40S for background/batch jobs to cut cost.

Ask from you before sizing workshop (quick):
- Confirm peak TPS and sustained TPS (per minute or 5-min window).
- Provide a simple token-length distribution (percent short/medium/long).
- Confirm whether VPC-only or private on-prem is required for the project.

Next steps I propose:
- 60-minute sizing workshop with Karthik (inference) and our security lead to walk the capacity worksheet and SOC2 questions.
- I attached the Redwood capacity worksheet and the SOC2 questionnaire for you to scan.
- Proposed times: Tuesday 2027-07-20 09:00-10:00 PT OR Wednesday 2027-07-21 11:00-12:00 PT. Which works?

Attachments: redwood-capacity-worksheet.xlsx (attached)

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Oliver — thanks for the numbers, that's very helpful. Quick preliminary sizing notes based on 75% short / 20% medium / 5% long and the traffic you shared: 

Preliminary Dedicated sizing (ballpark):
- Day-to-day: 2x A100 80GB instances should comfortably cover ~60 sustained TPS with good headroom for batching.
- Peak bursts: to hit the ~220 TPS 5-min peak with low p95 latency, we'd recommend either 3x H100 80GB or a mixed pool: 2x H100 + 3x A100 where H100s serve interactive, latency-sensitive routes and A100s handle background and mid-latency endpoints.

Concurrency and batch tuning:
- For ~200-512 token median context, estimate 8-12 concurrent streams per A100 when using dynamic batching; H100 supports higher concurrency and longer contexts.
- KV cache for repeat prefixes (routing prompts) can reduce per-request compute by 15-30% depending on hit rate.

Cost/ops notes:
- Quantized 4-bit runtimes on A100/L40S give large cost savings for short-token workloads; we can show a comparative table in the workshop.
- Private VPC + KMS is straightforward on Dedicated; we'll include network topology examples for your security team.

Next steps from infra side:
- We'll formalize these into two scenarios (Cost-optimized and Performance-optimized) and bring estimated monthly $/token numbers.
- Confirmed workshop: 2027-07-21 11:00 PT — Karthik (inference), Vanessa (solutions), Ben (sales) + Redwood security lead to be added.

Please confirm attendees and we'll send an agenda + pre-reads (capacity worksheet + short checklist on tokens and SLAs).

Thanks,
